summary: Conservative engine map for the vehicle_ai_and_pit scope reconciled from three independent validated proposals (vehicle_ai_and_pit_01, wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_01, wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_02). The three proposals describe overlapping but complementary regions of the same subsystem: a per-frame vehicle AI tick orchestrated by AIMainUpdate (0x00424E70) that gates on the aiEnable flag, runs racing-line/steering/pit decision helpers, and commits control outputs; a fixed 400-tick main loop (0x0042C690) that drives the AI tick; an AI command queue (0x00424CD0) with deduplicated 8-byte {command,value} entries; pit-entry/exit strategy (0x0042A110, 0x0042A3D0, 0x0042AD50); a CONFIRMED-owner pit machine cluster (0x004A5D10/0x004A5FA0/0x004A6200/0x004A68B0); and a tire-physics object (0x004E4500/0x004E88B0/0x004E8CE0/0x004E9100/0x004E9300/0x004EE150/0x004EFAE0/0x004F1510/0x004F68B0) with a racing-line tracker. The this-based F1CVehicle AI/pit field block is emitted as one family merged from two proposals (11 methods, cross-proposal calls and shared field offsets), while the obj-base vehicle root (proposal class wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_02:6, same name) is kept as a separate GUESS family per the no-merge rule. Six state machines, ten interfaces, and all 21 source contracts are preserved. Contradictions (this+0x32C8 naming, this+0x454C dual role, this+0x4550 dual semantics, this+0x45E0 triple use, 0x0042A110 name, dword_7CEA5C mode range, F1CVehicle identity split, tire-system split) are recorded in conflicts, not erased. Trust limited to DERIVED/GUESS/UNKNOWN.

engine_subsystems.name: VehicleAIAndPit
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Per-frame AI decision-making and pit-stop strategy/timing for race vehicles: AI tick orchestration gated on the aiEnable flag (AIMainUpdate 0x00424E70) with pre-race/formation init and racing branches; waypoint/racing-line following, steering-target computation and lane scoring; a driver-status state machine (0..7); AI ability drift and difficulty scaling; AI command-queue dispatch; pit-entry/exit forcing, tire-compound pit-stop scheduling and retirement; a fixed 400-tick main loop (0x0042C690); the CONFIRMED-owner pit machine cluster (mode dispatch, pit-box alignment, readiness, per-frame servicing with speed limiter and wheel-force ramps); and per-vehicle/per-wheel tire physics, tire-brand lookup, opponent roster building and racing-line path traversal. The three proposal names (VehicleAIPitControl, VehicleAIAndPit, VehicleAIAndPitOperations) name overlapping regions of one scope, connected by cross-proposal calls (0x0042C690 -> 0x00424E70; 0x00424E70 -> steering/racing-line helpers; 0x0042A3D0 called by both 0x00429470 and 0x004A6200).

canonical_type_families.name: F1CVehicle
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Race vehicle AI/pit field container: the per-vehicle AI field block (this base, roughly +0x4000..+0x461C) plus shared vehicle fields (position/velocity/heading at +0x34E0..+0x34F8, committed input at +0x357C/+0x3580/+0x3584, aiEnable flag +0x32C8, driverStatus +0x4510, pit flags +0x4548/+0x454C/+0x45F4, command queue +0x44A8..+0x44B0, retirement +0x4410). Merged from two source proposals: both name the same this-base block, their methods share call relationships (0x00424E70 calls the steering/racing-line set; 0x00429470 calls 0x0042A3D0; 0x0042A110 calls 0x0042AC70) and shared field offsets (this+0x32C8, +0x454C, +0x44A8, +0x45F4). The obj base (vehicle root reached via this+0) is kept distinct per the no-merge rule; see F1CVehicleSubObject.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Field samples are boundary clues, not a complete layout: the 158/63 field counts of the two source proposals are provisional. this-base and obj-base stay distinct even though obj+0x32C8 and this+0x32C8 are the same physical offset with conflicting names (aiEnableFlag / onTrackFlag / AiPitSubState) - recorded as a conflict. Dual-role offsets this+0x454C, this+0x4550 and triple-use this+0x45E0 keep their proposal names until a named struct or poke decides. AIDriverStructInit (0x00424790) reinitialises the whole block per session.

Carries the vehicle sub-state obj+0x32C8 (pit dispatch values 2/3), finish state obj+0x4064, AI reason code obj+0x4068 (value 9 cleared at pit exit), step flag obj+0x4094, target node id obj+0x4040, velocity/wheel-spin vectors obj+0x34C4..0x3500, pit-box index obj+0x48A4, and pit-crew mesh flag obj+0x105C. canonical_type_families.field_policy: obj-base field samples are boundary clues from the pit machine and racing-line tracker. obj+0x32C8 is the same physical offset as this+0x32C8 (conflict recorded). No methods are assigned because the proposal lists none; ownership of the pit-machine/tracker read patterns stays with the reading families.

state_machines.name: DriverStatusMachine
transitions: pit-wait timer 0x4170 < now -> driverStatus = 4 (session type 0x7C56A4==7) else 5, then re-arm pit-exit timer 0x447C
0/6 -> SteeringAngleController (0x425670); 6 -> 7 when |heading error| < 0.5 or 0x447C elapsed
0x447C snapshot timer -> toggle 6/0 and snapshot position into 0x4470/0x4474/0x4478
1 -> sub_4258C0; 2 -> FieldZeroSetter and return; 3 -> waypoint squared-distance vs 0x461C -> 0 when farther, else update 0x461C
steering-error accumulator 0x446C > 0x4558 -> driverStatus = 1 (after RaceStartCountdownStateUpdate when gear 0x39FC > 2)
7 -> zero 0x442C/0x4438/0x4434; Speed 0x4440 < 0.2 -> driverStatus = 0
racing-line reset path -> driverStatus = 4/5 by 0x7C56A4; pit-return 5 -> 3 after tier selection or -> 0

state_machines.name: PitStopDecisionMachine
transitions: PitStopBlockingCondition or session != 7 -> not service-ready; when session==7 set RetiredFlag 0x4410=1, clear AIControlFlag 0x45F4, log via sub_4BC060
service-ready path -> tire-compound tier selection and SpeedValueSetterWithGlobalMirror + PostPitCleanup

state_machines.name: AIPitStateMachine
transitions: Idle -> PitRequested: AI command id 1 schedules the pit decision timer (this+0x413C = session time + 2.0)
PitRequested -> PitLaneActive: AI command id 4 enables the pit state via sub_4A46F0(this, 1, 1)
PitLaneActive -> Idle: AI command id 5 clears this+0x4548 and disables the pit state via sub_4A46F0(this, 0, 0)
Idle -> PitRequested: pit-window phase (dword_7C56A8 == 5) with a sub-1 fuel multiplier forces a pit exit (ForcePitExit)
Any -> Blocked: last-lap, teammate-part, or finish-state guard blocks ForcePitExit
Any -> Blocked: race phase dword_7C56A8 == 8 blocks pit requests (PitStopBlockingCondition)

state_machines.name: AICommandQueue
transitions: Idle -> Pending: append an 8-byte {command, value} entry at +0x44A8 and store the new index at +0x44B0
Pending -> Pending: re-send the queued response when the command is already present (dedup scan)
Pending -> Idle: after CommandQueueResponseHandler (0x00429EE0), the index at +0x44B0 resets to -1
Pending -> Full: append denied when index + 1 reaches capacity +0x44AC; the index is restored to its previous value

state_machines.name: PitMachineState
transitions: Event mode byte at a2+8 differs from this+0x184 -> store it and call AIPitStrategyState on the base vehicle
Vehicle sub-state obj+0x32C8 == 2 or 3 -> dispatch on mode this+0x184 (2 -> sub_4A5EA0, 0 -> sub_4A5F20)
PitMid flag fires in the last 2.0s before completion (this+0x1A4)
StateChangeNotify(state 4) leaves the pit stop
AI reason code obj+0x4068 == 9 cleared to 0 when the limiter deactivates

state_machines.name: EngineWearMode
transitions: Four wear slots +0x3D64..0x3D70 initialized to FLT_MAX before any mode check
Wear recompute runs per frame when dword_7CEA5C in (0, 2]
Wear value divided by flt_8ACF9C when dword_7C56A4 == 7 and dword_7CEA5C == 2
TireScrubReset clamps wear slot +0x3D64 (or global dbl_7C91DC) gated by dword_7CEA5C
